title: Ember and Oath Anew
premise: Lior Hartwell, youngest oath-keeper of the Ember Guild, has spent her life in the Hollow Valley, a place where magic cannot follow and where her guild hides the last free souls in jars of ash. When the usurper King Vessic declares a hunt for the gifted, Lior learns her own brother's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain years ago to buy the valley's safety. Leaving home for the first time, she gathers a found family of hunted misfits—a disgraced court mage, a memory-thief, and a soldier who deserted the hunt—and crosses the war-torn free cities to reach the Undercourt before Vessic's armies seal it forever. In the mountain's heart, Lior discovers she herself is the vessel holding her brother's stolen soul, and that reclaiming him means surrendering every memory of who she is. She chooses to give them up, waking as a stranger among friends who refuse to let her forget them, while the freed souls ignite a rebellion that topples Vessic.
about_author: L. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from communities displaced by border wars, an experience that shapes their fiction's obsession with what survives when memory fails. They write fantasy about chosen families from a small house at the edge of a large forest, accompanied by two opinionated cats.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She tends the guild's ash-jars on the eve of the Founding Festival, establishing the valley where magic cannot follow and her role as its youngest keeper. Beat: quiet belonging shadowed by restlessness.

chapters.title: Oath of Ash
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Ember Guild swears its annual oath; Elder Maren hints that the guild once paid a terrible price for the valley's protection. Beat: reverence laced with unease.

chapters.title: The Crier's Bell
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A royal crier arrives announcing the Gift Hunt—every gifted person must be registered or burned. The valley's wards flicker for the first time in a century. Beat: dread arriving like weather.

chapters.title: What Maren Buried
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The elder reveals a ledger page: a soul was sold to the Undercourt twenty years ago to buy the valley's invisibility—the name on the page is Hartwell. Beat: guilt finally surfacing.

chapters.title: My Brother's Name
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She confronts Maren and learns Tam, the brother she barely remembers, was traded away—and that Lior carries something of his she cannot name. Beat: grief for a memory she never had.

chapters.title: Leaving Is a Kind of Dying
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The guild votes to stay hidden; Lior vows to go alone. Maren gives her Tam's old compass and a warning: the road remembers what the valley cannot hold. Beat: severance and resolve.

chapters.title: The First Mile
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Outside the valley, magic rushes back into her—dangerous, loud, visible. She narrowly escapes a hunt patrol using a trick she didn't know she knew. Beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Sells Yesterday
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A memory-thief named Sable catches Lior stealing bread and offers partnership: she knows the roads to the Undercourt and wants a soul of her own back. Beat: wary transactional sparks.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Are Burning Slowly
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the city of Corren's Landing, they witness a public burning of a gifted child's family. Lior's magic flares involuntarily; Sable drags her clear. Beat: horror hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Mage Without a Court
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. Disgraced court mage Iven Ashgrave, hiding in a smuggler's den, recognizes the ember-mark on Lior's wrist—a mark only Undercourt vessels bear. Beat: recognition that changes everything.

chapters.title: Vessel
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. Iven explains: Lior isn't just Tam's sister; she may be the living jar that holds his soul. Lior refuses to believe it until her reflection shows her brother's eyes. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: A Soldier Who Missed
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Hunt-captain Dara Ferro deliberately misses her shot at Lior, then deserts, following the trio. She carries a list of names she refuses to finish. Beat: conscience over orders.

chapters.title: Four Against the Road
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The mismatched four argue over trust, then survive an ambush by Vessic's hounds together. Something like family begins, unspoken. Beat: friction annealing into loyalty.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable trades a stolen memory of her mother to a ferry-wight for passage, revealing how much she has already given away. Lior promises never to ask her to trade again. Beat: sacrifice witnessed.

chapters.title: Letters We Never Sent
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Camped in ruins, each shares one true thing: Iven's betrayal of his students, Sable's sold childhood, Dara's unfinished list, Lior's fear of forgetting Tam again. Beat: vulnerability as glue.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. Vessic announces the Undercourt will be sealed at midwinter; all souls within become crown property. The deadline becomes the book's ticking clock. Beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: City of Salt and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the free city of Vell, they find a hidden network of the gifted led by an old friend of Maren's—who tells them the only way into the Undercourt is to be sold into it. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Price of Entry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. To enter as merchandise, Lior must let Sable take her memories of the journey so no interrogator can read them. She agrees, terrified. Beat: trust as an act of courage.

chapters.title: What Sable Took
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inside Sable's mind we see Lior's taken memories—including a moment Lior called the group her family. Sable weeps alone. Beat: love stored where it can't be felt.

chapters.title: Sold South
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Dara poses as a bounty driver delivering Lior to the mountain gate; the others infiltrate as laborers. The gate's warden reads Lior's empty mind and waves them through. Beat: cold triumph.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Undercourt: a cathedral of jars, each holding a soul, lit by ember-light identical to the guild's. Lior realizes the valley's magic wasn't banished—it was harvested here. Beat: awe curdling into fury.

chapters.title: The Broker of Names
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. Iven bargains with the soul-broker, his former mentor, buying time with secrets. He learns Vessic plans to drink the jars' power at midwinter. Beat: old sins negotiating with new ones.

chapters.title: Tam
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior finds Tam's jar—but it is empty. The broker laughs: the soul was placed in a vessel long ago and walked out on its own legs. Beat: the floor dropping away.

chapters.title: The Mirror Corridor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Guided by her ember-mark, Lior reaches the vessel vault and faces a mirror showing Tam's face overlaid on hers. The truth lands: she is the vessel; she has been both siblings all along. Beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Lie
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (interlude). Back in the valley, Maren burns the guild ledger and confesses to the guild that Lior was created—soul-bound—as a container, and sent to the valley to be kept safe from knowing. Beat: tragic guardianship revealed.

chapters.title: Reclaiming
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. To free Tam, Lior must open herself and release him—which will strip her memories as he takes back his own. Her friends arrive mid-ritual and beg her to stop. Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Ember and Oath Anew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. Midwinter bells ring as Vessic's army seals the gates above. Lior speaks a new oath—not the guild's, but her own—and opens the vessel. Tam rises; her memories pour out like light. Beat: self-sacrifice as triumph.

chapters.title: The Jars Break
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Freed and furious, Tam shatters the vault; hundreds of souls return to their bodies across the mountain, and the re-gifted rise against the garrison. Beat: liberation as wildfire.

chapters.title: The King Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. Vessic arrives to drink the jars and finds them broken; Iven duels his former king's sorcerers while Dara's deserters turn their ballistae on the throne guard. Beat: debts collected.

chapters.title: Who Is Lior Hartwell?
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Awake but emptied, Lior knows nothing—not her name, not the strangers weeping over her who insist they are her family. Beat: the cost made intimate.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable returns Lior's journey memories one fragment at a time, refusing to keep even one for herself. Lior relearns her friends' names like prayers. Beat: found family rebuilding identity.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Home
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The company escorts the freed gifted out of the collapsing mountain as Vessic's army routs. Dara finally finishes her list—by crossing out every name still alive. Beat: exhaustion and grace.

chapters.title: Ash and Snow
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, guilty at the price of his freedom, tries to leave; Lior stops him. They are not the siblings they were, but they begin again as what they are now. Beat: forgiveness without erasure.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The company reaches the Hollow Valley, where the wards have fallen because the harvest has ended. Magic floods the valley for the first time in a century. Beat: home transformed.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Guild
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren kneels before Lior and offers her the elder's staff and her own exile. Lior refuses both: the guild must change, not scatter. Beat: mercy stronger than punishment.

chapters.title: A New Oath
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Ember Guild rewrites its oath—from hiding the gifted to sheltering them openly. Lior, now elder-in-all-but-name, leads the first swearing under open sky. Beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: Hunters No More
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Word comes that Vessic is deposed and the Gift Hunt dissolved; Dara burns her captain's insignia and asks to stay in the valley as its sword. Beat: the soldier finding where she belongs.

chapters.title: Everything Sable Kept
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable gives Lior the final fragment: the campfire moment when Lior called them family. Lior says it aloud again, this time with all of them listening. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Left
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the valley's edge, Lior buries Tam's compass beside a new marker stone reading 'both of us.' She looks down the road she once feared and feels no pull to follow it. Beat: peace after becoming.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. One year later: the valley glows with trained, shared magic; the guild trains the displaced; Lior teaches children whose names no ledger will ever sell. Final line echoes the opening oath, rewritten. Beat: full-circle resolution.
